verified_reason: E06: Juhn & Tarnopolsky 1998 is a narrative 'critical review'. The only method stated is a keyword Medline search; there are no eligibility criteria, no selection process and no count of included studies, and it draws on abstracts and animal studies. Weaker than the SP1-0637 precedent (4 named databases, 19 selected articles), so not an SR/MA mapping record. Citation-chasing source for pre-1998 side-effect reports

Poortmans & Francaux 1999: cross-sectional comparison of long-term creatine users (10 months to 5 y) with a control group; creatinine, urea and albumin clearances (eligible renal markers; non-randomised, so safety only, ROBINS-I). Same design as SP1-0116, which was included, but the abstract gives no age, no training type (RT or other) and no description of the controls. Full text not open in Europe PMC; decide at full text

Robinson 2000: RCT, 48 young healthy subjects, creatine 20 g/d for 5 d up to 3 g/d for 9 wk; renal, hepatic and haematological indices (eligible renal markers, 9 wk arm meets the 4 wk minimum). The abstract mentions no exercise programme at all, so E03 is the likely outcome, but RT is the only open criterion and only the full text settles it. Full text (PMC1724224, PDF only) could not be opened. Renal-safety context if excluded

Shi 2005: creatine and/or oligosaccharide vs placebo, 2x2 design, 20 male basketball players (5 per group, allocation method not stated); glucose, lactate, urea nitrogen and CK measured after competition. Reads as an acute recovery study (likely E05 or E07), but duration and training are not stated and urea is a listed renal marker. Full text not open in Europe PMC; decide at full text. Low prior of eligibility

Cancela 2008: double-blind RCT, CrM (15 g/d for 7 d then 3 g/d for 49 d) vs maltodextrin, 14 football players, 8 wk; blood and urine renal and hepatic markers, body mass. Abstract says only 'football-specific training'; whether that included a structured RT programme is not stated (E03 if sport-only). Same situation as SP1-0255, which was kept as maybe. Full text not open in Europe PMC; decide at full text
E03: observational diet-pattern study with an acute step-exercise test; no creatine supplementation
E03: SR/MA of accentuated eccentric loading vs constant-load RT; no creatine
E03: 12-wk in-season strength training in female soccer players; no creatine (sample aged 14.9 y, so E02 also applies)
E02: adolescent girls with overweight or obesity, HIIT; no creatine
E02: children with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, retrospective cohort
E03: acute RT session to failure vs non-failure, crossover, 6 trained men; no creatine
E06: single case report of nutritional periodisation in a boxer; creatine kinase only as a marker
E02: idiopathic inflammatory myopathies, retrospective single-centre cohort
E03: GATM genetic variants and creatinine-based eGFR in population cohorts; no creatine supplementation
E02: postmenopausal women (Women's Health Initiative), D3-creatine tracer for muscle mass; no supplementation
E06: single case study of a 49-year-old ultra-endurance runner
E02: two paediatric immune-mediated necrotising myopathy cases (E06 also applies)
E06: two case reports of exercise-induced aminotransferase elevation
E03: methodological appraisal of the D3-creatine dilution method; tracer, no supplementation (E06 also applies)
E02: Cochrane review of all pharmacological and nutritional treatments for McArdle disease; multi-treatment review of a disease, not creatine-specific (convention)
E03: SR/MA of probiotics in chronic kidney disease; no creatine supplementation (serum creatinine is an outcome)
E01: meta-analysis in laying hens
E03: creatine plus multivitamin vs multivitamin for 4 wk in healthy volunteers, no exercise programme; homocysteine only (E05 also applies)
E02: ALS patients, mean age 57.7 y, creatine 10 g/d vs placebo for about 310 days, no RT. Adverse-event context only (urea, urinary albumin, GI events)

E03 confirmed: Gualano 2008, creatine about 10 g/d vs dextrose placebo for 3 months, 18 sedentary men aged 18-35, with moderate aerobic training only (3 x 40 min/wk). Protocol 2 requires a structured RT programme and protocol 3 names endurance-only training under E03. Keep as renal-safety context: one of the few RCTs with cystatin C (0.82 to 0.71 mg/L creatine vs 0.88 to 0.75 mg/L placebo at 12 wk). Indirect evidence only, not pooled

E04 confirmed at full text (PMC12968080): phase II had two arms only, micronized vs marketed creatine monohydrate (n=26 each), creatine in both, no placebo or no-creatine arm (one stray use of 'placebo group' in the results text is a wording error). Participants kept habitual RT, not a structured programme
E06: EFSA regulatory opinion on a health claim, assessing studies submitted by the applicant; not an SR/MA with its own search, and the conclusion concerns adults over 55. Citation-chasing source

E03: Earnest 1996, creatine vs glucose placebo for 56 d in 34 hypercholesterolaemic men and women aged 32-70, no RT (physical activity unchanged); lipids, urea nitrogen, creatinine (E02 also applies). Different sample from SP2-0336 (weight-trained men), so not a companion

E02: SR of exercise plus seven different supplements in type 2 diabetes patients; multi-supplement review of a disease, not creatine-specific. Citation-chasing source for its one creatine plus training renal trial
E03: creatine 20 g/d plus glucose vs glucose in 18 sprinters, loading only, sprint training with no RT programme; sprint performance outcomes only (E05 and E07 also apply)
E03: Poortmans 1997, 5-day creatine loading vs placebo in 5 men, no exercise programme; renal responses (E07 also applies, below 4 wk). Renal-safety context
E04: single-arm, creatine 5 g/d for one month in 11 active sportsmen, no control group; homocysteine and urinary metabolites

SR/MA mapping: creatine-specific systematic review (PRISMA, PubMed only, 5 studies: 3 RCTs and 2 cohorts). Full text (PMC13158627) checked: criteria are creatine monohydrate with safety outcomes, RCTs and cohorts eligible, no exclusion of RT co-interventions. The adolescent restriction is a population criterion, which does not count under the rule as clarified at 12:28. Low yield expected for our 18-50 population; weak review (single database, no risk-of-bias assessment)

Kreider 2003: open-label, self-selected creatine vs non-creatine supplements over 21 months in 98 Division IA football players 'undergoing intense training'; 69-item blood and urine panel including renal markers. Non-randomised, so safety outcomes only (ROBINS-I). RT is not named in the abstract; confirm at full text. Not the same cohort as SP1-0116 (Mayhew 2002: Division II, n=23, cross-sectional users vs non-users). Likely companions are the Greenwood 2003 injury reports (SP8-0047; PMID 12701814, not in records.csv)

SR/MA mapping: Lopez 2009, creatine-specific SR/MA of RCTs (5 databases, PEDro appraisal, 10 studies) on heat tolerance and hydration. Under the SR/MA rule outcomes do not count, and the criteria stated in the abstract (RCTs of creatine supplementation with hydration or thermoregulation outcomes) do not rule out an RT co-intervention. Full text could not be opened to read the exclusion criteria; recode E05 if they restrict to acute exercise-in-heat trials
